+import ast
+
+import pytest
+
+from jinja2 import Environment
+from jinja2 import nodes
+from jinja2.compiler import DependencyFinderVisitor
+
+
+SOURCE = (
+    "{{ value|root_f }}{{ value is root_t }}"
+    "{% block outer %}"
+    "{{ value|outer_f }}{{ value is outer_t }}"
+    "{% block inner %}"
+    "{{ value|inner_f }}{{ value is inner_t }}"
+    "{% endblock %}"
+    "{% endblock %}"
+)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", [None, False, True])
+def test_inventory_modes(mode):
+    tree = Environment().parse(SOURCE)
+    visitor = (
+        DependencyFinderVisitor()
+        if mode is None
+        else DependencyFinderVisitor(include_blocks=mode)
+    )
+    visitor.visit(tree)
+    expected = {"root"}
+    if mode is True:
+        expected.update(("outer", "inner"))
+    assert visitor.filters == {f"{name}_f" for name in expected}
+    assert visitor.tests == {f"{name}_t" for name in expected}
+
+
+def test_block_entry_boundaries():
+    tree = Environment().parse(SOURCE)
+    block = next(tree.find_all(nodes.Block))
+    default = DependencyFinderVisitor()
+    default.visit(block)
+    assert default.filters == set()
+    assert default.tests == set()
+    whole = DependencyFinderVisitor(include_blocks=True)
+    whole.visit(block)
+    assert whole.filters == {"outer_f", "inner_f"}
+    assert whole.tests == {"outer_t", "inner_t"}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("include_blocks", [False, True])
+def test_expression_children(include_blocks):
+    tree = Environment().parse(
+        "{{ (x|lower) is equalto(y|upper) }}"
+        "{{ x|default(y is defined) }}"
+    )
+    visitor = DependencyFinderVisitor(include_blocks=include_blocks)
+    visitor.visit(tree)
+    assert visitor.filters == {"lower", "upper", "default"}
+    assert visitor.tests == {"equalto", "defined"}
+
+
+def test_compilation_dependency_scopes():
+    env = Environment(optimized=False)
+    for prefix in ("root", "outer", "inner"):
+        env.filters[f"{prefix}_f"] = lambda value: value
+        env.tests[f"{prefix}_t"] = lambda value: True
+    module = ast.parse(env.compile(SOURCE, raw=True))
+    functions = {
+        node.name: node
+        for node in module.body
+        if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef)
+    }
+    for function, prefix in (
+        ("root", "root"),
+        ("block_outer", "outer"),
+        ("block_inner", "inner"),
+    ):
+        dependencies = set()
+        for node in ast.walk(functions[function]):
+            if (
+                isinstance(node, ast.Subscript)
+                and isinstance(node.value, ast.Attribute)
+                and isinstance(node.value.value, ast.Name)
+                and node.value.value.id == "environment"
+                and node.value.attr in {"filters", "tests"}
+            ):
+                assert isinstance(node.slice, ast.Constant)
+                dependencies.add((node.value.attr, node.slice.value))
+        assert dependencies == {
+            ("filters", f"{prefix}_f"),
+            ("tests", f"{prefix}_t"),
+        }

spec.question:
Expose a whole-tree inventory mode on `jinja2.compiler.DependencyFinderVisitor` by adding an `include_blocks=False` constructor option. With the option enabled, visiting a template or a block must collect filter and test names from all descendants, including nested blocks, into the existing `filters` and `tests` sets. Dependencies in filter and test arguments must still be included. With the option omitted or explicitly false, preserve the current behavior of stopping at every block boundary.

This is an inventory capability, not a change to compilation: `CodeGenerator.pull_dependencies` must retain the default mode, and generated root and block functions must continue initializing only their own dependencies, excluding those belonging to nested block functions. Leave `NodeVisitor.get_visitor` unchanged. Return a unified diff against production files only; do not modify tests.

suggestion.behavior_shift: Expands the evidence path from a focused dispatch module to a visitor and its compilation consumers. Selective reading of dependency collection and root/block generation is useful for preserving the existing default while testing the new traversal mode; repository-wide investigation or forced recursion is unnecessary.
suggestion.description: Add an opt-in whole-tree dependency inventory to src/jinja2/compiler.py::DependencyFinderVisitor. Introduce an include_blocks=False constructor option; when true, visit_Block must traverse the block's children so that filters and tests inside nested blocks are collected. The default must continue stopping at blocks. Keep CodeGenerator.pull_dependencies using the default behavior, since CodeGenerator.visit_Template separately collects dependencies for root and block functions. Deliver a unified diff with acceptance tests covering dependencies outside blocks, inside blocks, and inside nested blocks, plus a check that ordinary compilation retains separate root and block dependency initialization. Do not change src/jinja2/visitor.py::NodeVisitor.get_visitor.
suggestion.expected_answer_change: The implementation depends on DependencyFinderVisitor.__init__, DependencyFinderVisitor.visit_Block, and its existing visit_Filter and visit_Test traversal. Compatibility evidence comes from CodeGenerator.pull_dependencies and the separate root and block calls in CodeGenerator.visit_Template. The verified patch changes compiler.py rather than the default visitor dispatcher.
suggestion.why_substantive: This changes a concrete compiler visitor's traversal boundary and exposes a new inventory mode, rather than changing family-handler dispatch. Correctness requires understanding why the existing block boundary is intentional and why enabling the new mode globally in the compiler would alter generated dependency initialization.
